title.value: Stochastic Polyak Step-size for SGD: An Adaptive Learning Rate for Fast Convergence
title.justification: The title was explicitly mentioned multiple times throughout the paper, such as at the beginning and in the conclusion.
title.quote: Stochastic Polyak Step-size for SGD: An Adaptive Learning Rate for Fast Convergence

analysis.description: The paper proposes a novel adaptive learning rate called the stochastic Polyak step-size (SPS) for Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD). The SPS is a variant of the classical Polyak step-size adapted to the stochastic setting, which provides fast convergence rates without needing problem-dependent constants or additional computational overhead. The authors provide theoretical convergence guarantees for SPS-equipped SGD in various contexts including convex, non-convex, and strongly-convex problems. Additionally, the paper discusses the efficacy of SPS in training over-parameterized models and validates the theoretical results through experiments on synthetic and real datasets.

type.justification: The paper extensively provides theoretical analysis and convergence guarantees for the stochastic Polyak step-size in different mathematical settings such as convex, non-convex, and strongly-convex contexts, which indicates a theoretical contribution.
type.quote: We provide theoretical guarantees for the convergence of SGD with SPS in different scenarios including strongly convex, convex and non-convex smooth functions.

name.justification: The research primarily contributes to the field of optimization in machine learning by proposing an adaptive learning rate method for SGD, which is a core optimization technique in this field.
name.quote: Stochastic gradient descent (SGD) (Robbins and Monro, 1951; Nemirovski and Yudin, 1978, 1983; Shalev-Shwartz et al., 2007; Nemirovski et al., 2009; Hardt et al., 2016), is the workhorse for training supervised machine learning problems.

name.justification: The paper discusses the effectiveness of the proposed learning rate method in training deep neural networks, and includes experiments on deep learning architectures, implying its relevance to the deep learning field.
name.quote: More recently, adaptive methods (Duchi et al., 2011; Liu et al., 2019; Kingma and Ba, 2015; Bengio, 2015; Vaswani et al., 2019b; Li and Orabona, 2019; Ward et al., 2019) that adjust the step-size on the fly have become wide-spread and are particularly beneficial when training deep neural networks.

name.justification: The paper introduces the stochastic Polyak step-size (SPS), a modification of SGD, as its main contribution and extensively analyzes its theoretical properties.
name.quote: We propose a novel adaptive learning rate for SGD. The proposed step-size is a natural extension of the Polyak step-size to the stochastic setting. We name it stochastic Polyak step-size (SPS).

is_contributed.justification: The SPS is the central proposed method of the paper, constituting a new contribution to the field of optimization in machine learning.
is_contributed.quote: We propose a novel adaptive learning rate for SGD.

is_executed.justification: While the theoretical aspects of SPS are presented, there is no specific mention of the model being executed on GPU or CPU within the context of the paper.
is_executed.quote: We propose a novel adaptive learning rate for SGD.

is_compared.justification: The paper compares the performance of SGD with SPS against other state-of-the-art optimization methods, including numerical comparisons in experiments.
is_compared.quote: We experimentally validate our theoretical results via experiments on synthetic and real datasets. We demonstrate the strong performance of SGD with SPS compared to state-of-the-art optimization methods when training over-parameterized models.
